{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVlzVyc8AAAABixZbxw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BqjeczhMH_Ig", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bqjec", "number": 26, "title": "Simplify Cognix startup with persistent configuration and runtime command approval", "body": "## Goal

Make Cognix usable from a normal project directory by running `cognix`, without requiring users to configure command permissions or repeat model/runtime options on every launch.

## Current behavior

The CLI already has defaults (including the current directory as the project root), but a typical edit-and-verify session requires an explicit model selection and an exact `--allow-command` JSON argv for each permitted verification command. There is no persistent user configuration.

## Scope

- Provide a documented installation/launch path for `cognix` on the supported macOS environment. Keep the development launcher available.
- Keep sensible built-in defaults. Add an optional user-level TOML configuration (e.g. `~/.cognix/config.toml`) for model, Ollama URL, context size, step limits, and timeouts. Explicit CLI flags override environment settings and the config file; config values override built-in defaults. Preserve existing environment variable support.
- Allow the agent to propose a command at runtime without requiring an exact argv allowlist at startup. Show the actual command and ask for explicit approval before executing it. Keep the existing allowlist as an optional additional restriction for users who specify it.
- Preserve the existing command isolation, project boundaries, timeout/output limits, cancellation behavior, and fail-closed behavior. No shell expansion, unsandboxed fallback, or implicit approval; denied commands must not run. Keep the existing read-only project sandbox for command execution.
- Update the tool definition and system instructions to reflect the new runtime approval policy rather than requiring a predeclared command for every execution.

## Acceptance criteria

- After installation and with a usable local Ollama/model setup, running `cognix` from a project directory starts an interactive session without arguments.
- A saved model setting is used by default and can be overridden by `--model`; invalid configuration produces a clear error.
- The existing zero-division edit-and-verify example works without `--allow-command`: the agent proposes the test command, the user approves it at runtime, and the sandboxed test result is returned to the agent.
- Denial prevents execution, explicitly configured allowlists remain enforceable, and existing safety checks remain effective.
- Add focused tests for configuration precedence and command approval/restriction behavior, and update the README with the minimal startup and verification workflow.

Keep the implementation small. No new agent framework, generalized permission management system, or unrelated tool redesign is needed.", "url": "https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/issues/26", "created_at": "2026-11-26T14:11:14Z", "state": "OPEN", "repository": "takahirox/cognix", "labels": ["task"], "priority": null, "status": "In Progress", "is_archived": false}, "context": {}, "resources": {}, "allocation": {}, "instruction": null, "run_id": "4d3a4583ba7b49aab3bddb50ce4d86ba"}
